decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts extend the firm's core TGV and wafer-level packaging competence, and the R&D sunk into them is substantial, so management will keep them despite little visible promotion.
Carrier wafers are central to the announced direction of reusable carriers and thin-wafer handling, were launched publicly, and cost little to keep offering.

The Cu-interposer was publicly launched at SEMICON Europa as a flagship with heavy development investment, so dropping it would expose a visible strategic bet as a mistake, and any weak results can still be blamed on the pandemic and long semiconductor qualification cycles.
Wafer Universe is a publicly founded brand presented as a focus of the firm's direction, sits close to its established offer, and is cheap to sustain, so management keeps it.

Glass-based circuit boards are far from the core and were never committed to in public, which makes them the most likely candidate to drop, but they draw on the firm's glass structuring know-how and results can still be blamed on temporary market conditions, so management keeps them for now.
